evidence.claim: The Department of Atomic Energy says it was set up under the direct charge of the Prime Minister, which makes Modi's office directly relevant to atomic-energy governance in 2022.
evidence.title: History
evidence.excerpt: The Department of Atomic Energy says it was set up under the direct charge of the Prime Minister, which makes Modi's office directly relevant to atomic-energy governance in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government department history page; direct institutional authority claim.
evidence.period_fit: Long-running institutional structure that still applies in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional authority attaches to the PM office, not to a specific personal act by Modi.
contrary_evidence: This is structural authority, not evidence of a 2022 risk-bearing choice.

evidence.claim: India said the Arihant SLBM launch validated the SSBN programme and a robust survivable assured retaliatory capability consistent with its no-first-use posture.
evidence.title: INS Arihant carries out successful launch of Submarine Launched Ballistic Missile
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Defence
evidence.excerpt: India said the Arihant SLBM launch validated the SSBN programme and a robust survivable assured retaliatory capability consistent with its no-first-use posture.
evidence.source_locator: second and third paragraphs of the release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official 2022 government release on a nuclear-capability event.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level capability maintenance under Modi; it does not show a crisis decision or doctrinal change by him personally.
contrary_evidence: Strengthening retaliatory capability can stabilize deterrence, but it also continues modernization rather than disarmament.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that India did not explicitly condemn Russia's invasion, remained a major buyer of Russian oil, and that the decision not to hold the annual Modi-Putin summit was not due to the nuclear angle.
evidence.title: No Modi-Putin summit this year after they met in September- Indian govt source
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that India did not explicitly condemn Russia's invasion, remained a major buyer of Russian oil, and that the decision not to hold the annual Modi-Putin summit was not due to the nuclear angle.
evidence.source_locator: Reuters report text near the lead and second paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting carried by Euronews, with an explicit government-source attribution inside the report.
evidence.period_fit: Covers late-2022 statecraft around the Ukraine war.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Reports on Modi's broader diplomatic balancing, with one factual sentence directly attributed to an Indian government source.
contrary_evidence: India stayed strategically close to Russia on trade and energy even while urging restraint.

evidence.claim: Modi said the Ukraine-Russia conflict required an immediate cessation of violence and a return to direct dialogue and diplomacy as the only way forward.
evidence.title: Visit of the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom to India (April 21-22, 2022)
evidence.excerpt: Modi said the Ukraine-Russia conflict required an immediate cessation of violence and a return to direct dialogue and diplomacy as the only way forward.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official bilateral statement on the PMO site, dated in the target year.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 statement during the target year.
contrary_evidence: Again, this is rhetorical restraint rather than a demonstrable nuclear-risk reduction measure.

evidence.claim: The PMO said Modi reiterated that dialogue and diplomacy were the only way forward in the Ukraine conflict.
evidence.title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi speaks on telephone with His Excellency Mr Vladimir Putin, President of the Russian Federation
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Prime Minister's Office
evidence.excerpt: The PMO said Modi reiterated that dialogue and diplomacy were the only way forward in the Ukraine conflict.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official PMO readout of the call, dated in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler-level crisis messaging to a nuclear-armed counterpart.
contrary_evidence: It is a peace-oriented call, not proof of changes to command control or treaty posture.

evidence.claim: The UN First Committee record shows India abstained on the 2022 CTBT-related nuclear-disarmament text and on the broader nuclear-disarmament draft that called for a legally binding no-first-use instrument.
evidence.title: First Committee Sends 20 Nuclear Weapons Drafts to General Assembly Requiring 33 Separate Votes for Adoption
evidence.excerpt: The UN First Committee record shows India abstained on the 2022 CTBT-related nuclear-disarmament text and on the broader nuclear-disarmament draft that called for a legally binding no-first-use instrument.
evidence.source_locator: paragraphs describing the CTBT vote and the overall nuclear-disarmament draft
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN voting record with explicit country vote details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is the government's multilateral position under Modi, but not a personal statement by him.
contrary_evidence: India continued to advocate disarmament language even while withholding support from specific texts.

evidence.claim: India said it remained unwaveringly committed to universal, non-discriminatory, verifiable nuclear disarmament, supported a step-by-step multilateral framework, and backed measures to reduce nuclear danger, including de-alerting and de-targeting.
evidence.title: Statement by Ambassador DB Venkatesh Varma Permanent Representative of India to the CD during the Thematic Debate on Nuclear Weapons at First Committee
evidence.publisher: Permanent Mission of India to the Conference on Disarmament in Geneva
evidence.excerpt: India said it remained unwaveringly committed to universal, non-discriminatory, verifiable nuclear disarmament, supported a step-by-step multilateral framework, and backed measures to reduce nuclear danger, including de-alerting and de-targeting.
evidence.source_locator: opening and middle paragraphs of the statement
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Indian UN statement reproduced on the mission site; directly dated to the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government position under Modi; the statement is not personally by him but is attributable to his administration.
contrary_evidence: It is longstanding doctrine language and does not by itself prove new 2022 risk reduction on the ground.

evidence.claim: India said international transfers of dual-use goods and high-technology with military applications should be effectively regulated, and that it remained committed to an open, secure, stable, accessible, and peaceful cyberspace.
evidence.title: Statement by Mr. Maitrey Kulkarni, Deputy Secretary (D&ISA), Ministry of External Affairs, New Delhi at the CD Plenary on Aug 11, 2022 on 'The Centrality of International Cooperation and Capacity Building in Building Safe and Secure Cyberspace'
evidence.publisher: Permanent Mission of India to the Conference on Disarmament in Geneva
evidence.excerpt: India said international transfers of dual-use goods and high-technology with military applications should be effectively regulated, and that it remained committed to an open, secure, stable, accessible, and peaceful cyberspace.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official 2022 Indian statement on an emerging-catastrophic-risk domain, reproduced by the mission site.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 evidence for dual-use and cyber governance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government position under Modi; the speaker is an MEA official rather than Modi personally.
contrary_evidence: This is policy language, not proof of effective implementation or transparency in practice.

unresolved_gaps: No public 2022 evidence of a Modi-directed command-and-control reform, custody audit, launch-readiness change, or internal NCA practice change.
Personal attribution is thin for the more favorable multilateral statements and nuclear-governance positions.
The Russia balancing record is mostly government-level and UN-mission level rather than a clearly documented personal decision by Modi on oil, abstentions, or summit sequencing.
There is no 2022 external-combat or proxy-war exposure to test civilian-protection or proxy-control lenses in a strong way.
Direct Modi-level incitement evidence is thinner than the broader BJP and state-level abuse record.
The strongest custody-death and abuse claims still rely on NGO and U.S. State Department reporting with mixed central/state attribution.
Direct evidence of Modi personally directing electoral manipulation is thin relative to the stronger party-level and institutional record.
Several items show contestability and oversight but do not themselves prove that Modi strengthened democratic institutions in 2022.
Household-level and median-welfare evidence is thinner than the macro, capex, and program-count evidence.
Corruption, favoritism, and politically connected business privilege are underdeveloped relative to investment and growth material.
Independent outcome measures and subnational equity checks are still thin relative to the many ministry self-reports.
The current record is strong on inputs and service counts but weak on durable quality, learning, nutrition, and sustained poverty improvement.
No audited evidence of direct personal falsehood, correction, or hidden conflicts of interest has been recovered for 2022.
The negative items are mostly institutional opacity or noncooperation, not direct proof of personal self-dealing or a documented lie by Modi.
Project-level outcome audits and durability checks are still thinner than the program-design and rollout material.
Direct evidence that Modi replaced a specific ineffective implementer is absent.
